newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor says lifts S-E-Banken stake.
newsitem.headline: Investor says lifts S-E-Banken stake.

text.p: Swedish investment group Investor said it had bought shares in S-E-Banken worth 2.8 billion crowns in 1997, lifting its holding to 9.2 percent of capital and 9.6 percent of votes.

Investor's chief executive Claes Dahlback told the company's annual general meeting that Investor saw huge possibilities in the structural changes that are taking place in the financial markets all over the world.

"It's our intention as major holder in S-E-Banken to contribute toward appropriate structural changes, not least in the area of asset management, where we see significant possibilities for the future and where we in Investor have a solid tradition and sound knowledge," Dahlback said.
Investor is the investment vehicle of Sweden's powerful Wallenberg family which also set up and runs S-E-Banken.
During 1997 Investor also bought an additional one million shares in truck maker Scania, an additional 500,000 shares in telecoms group Ericsson and 550,000 shares in Swedish drugs major Astra.
"We continue actively to seek new investment opportunities inside and outside Sweden and have made a number of smaller investments during the spring," Dahlback said.
"At the same time we are expanding in our investment organisation, with offices in Hong Kong, London, New York and Stockholm."
Dahlback told the meeting that Investor's costs for consultation and listing truck group Scania in Sweden and the U.S. was about one billion crowns.
Investor sold off 55 percent of Scania and listed it separately in Stockholm and New York on April 1 lat year.
Dahlback was commenting on calculations made by Lars-Eric Forsgardh, chief executive of the Swedish shareholders' group Aktiespararna.
"Your calculations are close when saying it cost almost one billion crowns," Dahlback said.
